show: He sold his first stock too early. Guess who.
say: He sold his first stock too early. Guess who.
Nineteen forty-two. An eleven-year-old buys three shares for a hundred and fourteen dollars.
They drop to twenty-seven. He holds.
Then they climb past two hundred.

show: Charlie Munger: "The big money is not in the buying and the selling, but in the waiting."
say: Charlie Mungur. The big money is not in the buying and the selling, but in the waiting.

show: John Bogle: "Don't look for the needle in the haystack. Just buy the haystack!"
say: John Boagle. Don't look for the needle in the haystack. Just buy the haystack!

show: Buffett started with $114. A fund of your own? Usually $10,000 or more.
say: Buffett started with a hundred and fourteen dollars. A fund of your own? Usually ten thousand or more.
It should start at ten dollars.
